Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto-Ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, adapting the Spanish legal framework to EU directives; Ley 19/2021, de 20 de diciembre, establishing the Registro de Titularidades Reales; Directive (EU) 2018/843 (Fifth AML Directive) transposition measures; Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Mercantile Registry Regulations) and Circular 3/2022 of the Bank of Spain concerning corporate due diligence.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole Spanish registered office for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The mercantile registry requires a physical address within a Spanish municipality where the actual management or control is exercisable or, in accordance with Article 9 of Royal Decree 1784/1996, where a typical professional office can be inspected. A virtual address may be used only as an auxiliary mail-forwarding facility and must not be listed as the registered domicile in the incorporation deed.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the registered office's judicial province, e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid; Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate and BORME publication; Ministry of Justice (Ministerio de Justicia) as supervisory authority.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC) — Arts. 12-14 (minimum capital and paid-in rules), 20-22 (deed and registration), 28-39 (bylaws), 62 (subscription and payment), 137 (administration); Ley 18/2022, de 28 de septiembre, de creación y crecimiento de empresas (Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva regime); Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores (fast-track SL); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución (public incorporation deed) together with the Estatutos sociales (corporate bylaws), executed before a Spanish Notary and presented for inscription at the Registro Mercantil Provincial; preceded by certificación negativa de denominación social and followed by NIF assignment (Modelo 036) and mandatory publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 43 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Standard SL: minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid-in in cash at incorporation, evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit (certificado de depósito) per LSC Art. 62. Under the Ley 18/2022 SLFS regime, incorporation with capital below EUR 3,000 is permitted but distributions are restricted until such amount is reached and the company must allocate 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve. Capital contributions may not consist of services; increases or decreases require public deed and registry inscription.

Funding & unlock path:

Paid-in capital rule: Standard SL: minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid-in in cash at incorporation, evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit (certificado de depósito) per LSC Art. 62. Under the Ley 18/2022 SLFS regime, incorporation with capital below EUR 3,000 is permitted but distributions are restricted until such amount is reached and the company must allocate 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve. Capital contributions may not consist of services; increases or decreases require public deed and registry inscription.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Spanish State Tax Administration Agency; electronic headquarters: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

For an ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), obtain a provisional NIF through the notary/company registry prior to incorporation; after public deed and registration with the Mercantile Registry, file AEAT Modelo 036 to apply for definitive NIF and inscription in the official Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholders. A Spanish resident legal representative and a Spanish tax notification address are required. The NIF doubles as Spanish VAT ID when the company carries out taxable business activities; an EORI number must also be requested if goods exports are planned. For non-resident entities without a permanent establishment, direct VAT/NIF registration is made using Modelo 036 with the same electronic channel or through the applicable simplified registration forms; registration is required before any taxable supply in Spain.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: a Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxpayer fully liable to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income, with foreign tax relief; non-resident shareholders are subject only to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Spanish-source items. The SL is not pass-through eligible. — For an ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), obtain a provisional NIF through the notary/company registry prior to incorporation; after public deed and registration with the Mercantile Registry, file AEAT Modelo 036 to apply for definitive NIF and inscription in the official Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholders. A Spanish resident legal representative and a Spanish tax notification address are required. The NIF doubles as Spanish VAT ID when the company carries out taxable business activities; an EORI number must also be requested if goods exports are planned. For non-resident entities without a permanent establishment, direct VAT/NIF registration is made using Modelo 036 with the same electronic channel or through the applicable simplified registration forms; registration is required before any taxable supply in Spain.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: a Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxpayer fully liable to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income, with foreign tax relief; non-resident shareholders are subject only to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Spanish-source items. The SL is not pass-through eligible.

Available election forms

Spain has no check-the-box election. Available elections include: tax consolidation regime for groups meeting the 80% voting/equity threshold; accelerated depreciation; patent box regime for qualifying IP; merger/asset-contribution neutrality election; ETVE holding regime; SOCIMI listing election; and foreign tax credit rather than deduction election in some cases. Hybrid mismatch treatment under ATAD implementation is mandatory and cannot be eliminated by election.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general turnover threshold exists for Spanish-established suppliers: VAT registration via Modelo 036 is compulsory before commencing any business activity. For non-established EU sellers engaged in intra-EU distance sales or electronic services, the OSS registration threshold is EUR 10,000 if the seller is established in another Member State; for non-EU sellers any supply creates registration nexus.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Goods exports qualify for the export exemption with right to deduct input VAT (economically 0% IVA) where the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the European Union by the supplier, the customer, or a third party on their behalf, evidenced by the customs export declaration and transport documentation. Offshore and export-related services may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT or exempt where the recipient is established outside the EU under the B2B place-of-supply rules; the supplier must hold documentary evidence of the customer’s non-EU status, the nature of the service, and, where required, effective use and exploitation outside Spain.

  • Export Customs Declaration (DUA / Single Administrative Document) validated by Spanish Customs and evidencing definitive export from the EU
  • Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR road consignment note showing carriage out of the EU
  • Commercial invoice and export packing list
  • Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident purchaser
  • Exporter’s NIF/VAT ID and EORI registration evidence
  • Certificate of origin / EUR.1 or Form A where a preferential origin claim is made

Spain does not operate a transaction-by-transaction tax-stamping or pre-clearance model. The AEAT operates the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) requiring large taxpayers and VAT groups to submit invoice-level data electronically within 4 calendar days after issue; the B2C/B2B e-invoicing mandate is implemented through Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) using structured electronic invoice formats such as FacturaE XML. The VeriFactu framework requires billing software to generate tamper-evident, hash-linked invoice records accessible to AEAT. For public-sector invoices, the FACe platform and its API/interoperability requirements are mandatory.

AEAT rigorously audits export zero-rating files and may claw back deducted input VAT plus assess undeclared output VAT at 21% if export evidence is deficient, false, or not timely retained. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the VAT prejudice depending on concealment; late-payment interest accrues from the original due date; the four-year tax verification statute gives AEAT retrospective clawback power. Criminal liability under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code can apply (prison terms of 2–6 years) where defrauded VAT exceeds EUR 120,000. Exporters should retain the complete DUA/customs/B/L/payment record file for at least the statutory limitation period.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted within the euro area and generally unrestricted for cross-border commercial payments to third countries, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, payment-screening requirements, and bank documentation. Capital movements are liberalized under EU law and Spanish foreign-exchange legislation. An Spanish SL may generally receive foreign capital, hold foreign-currency accounts, pay foreign suppliers, distribute dividends, repay shareholder loans, and remit liquidation proceeds, provided corporate approvals, distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax requirements, beneficial-owner verification, transfer-pricing requirements, and applicable foreign-investment or external-transaction reporting are satisfied. Banks may require evidence of the capital contribution, loan agreement, dividend resolution, tax clearance or withholding evidence, source of funds, commercial rationale, and ultimate beneficial ownership before executing remittances. Foreign direct investment reporting may apply depending on investor status, ownership percentage, sector, transaction value, origin, and applicable statutory exemptions. Payments involving sanctioned persons, restricted jurisdictions, or unexplained third-party funds may be blocked or reported.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain does not impose a general statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank or convert a prescribed percentage of export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or foreign currency and may be received into Spanish or appropriately documented foreign accounts. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio or universal statutory repatriation deadline for ordinary goods exports. The company must retain commercial, customs, transport, invoice, and payment records and satisfy applicable VAT, Intrastat, statistical, banking, and anti-money-laundering information requests. Cash or equivalent instruments transported across EU external borders at EUR 10,000 or more must be declared under applicable EU and Spanish cash-control rules. Banks may impose contractual receipt, reconciliation, sanctions-screening, and documentary requirements, and sector-specific or state-support conditions may create additional reporting obligations.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-investment and external-payment reporting is also administered under the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, including the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investments.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium. An EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide EUR accounts, payment services, cards, and international transfers under passporting or local authorization, but it is not a Spanish deposit-taking bank unless separately licensed as a credit institution. Customer funds are generally safeguarded rather than covered by the Spanish deposit-guarantee scheme. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorization or a valid EU passport cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to the Spanish SL merely through an application interface. Fintech onboarding may be unsuitable for statutory share-capital certification, notarial incorporation evidence, complex shareholder loans, high-value trade finance, cash handling, documentary letters of credit, or transactions involving elevated sanctions, marketplace, or virtual-asset exposure. The company should maintain a regulated Spanish or EU bank as its primary treasury account and use an EMI only as a controlled secondary rail.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Unclear ownership chain, nominee shareholders, unexplained control rights, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.

Root cause: Unclear ownership chain, nominee shareholders, unexplained control rights, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.

Defense evidence: Certified current extract from the Spanish Commercial Registry; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart through every intermediate entity to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and proof of address for beneficial owners and directors; beneficial-owner declaration; powers of attorney; and explanation of voting and control arrangements.
Non-resident shareholder or director with documents that are expired, untranslated, unauthenticated, or inconsistent across jurisdictions.

Root cause: Non-resident shareholder or director with documents that are expired, untranslated, unauthenticated, or inconsistent across jurisdictions.

Defense evidence: Valid passports or national identity documents; recent address evidence; apostilled or legalized corporate certificates where required; sworn Spanish translations where requested; incumbency and good-standing certificates; board resolutions; notarized powers of attorney; and a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction identity reconciliation memorandum.
Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, unusually large initial deposits, or third-party funding.

Root cause: Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, unusually large initial deposits, or third-party funding.

Defense evidence: Executed subscription or loan agreement; shareholder and board approvals; bank statements showing the funding trail; audited financial statements or tax returns of the funding party; sale-of-asset or investment documentation where relevant; source-of-wealth narrative; sanctions screening; and a transaction-purpose statement tying the funds to incorporation, inventory, payroll, or operating expenditure.
Business model perceived as inconsistent with the stated activity, including robotics, artificial intelligence, consumer electronics, online sales, marketplaces, or high-volume card payments.

Root cause: Business model perceived as inconsistent with the stated activity, including robotics, artificial intelligence, consumer electronics, online sales, marketplaces, or high-volume card payments.

Defense evidence: Detailed business plan; product specifications; supplier and customer contracts; website and domain ownership evidence; warehouse or logistics agreements; distribution model; expected monthly transaction volumes; average ticket size; countries of operation; refund and chargeback policy; applicable product-safety and conformity documentation; and management experience profiles.
Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, restricted counterparties, unusual intermediaries, or mismatched payer and beneficiary names.

Root cause: Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, restricted counterparties, unusual intermediaries, or mismatched payer and beneficiary names.

Defense evidence: Counterparty KYC files; beneficial-owner evidence; contracts, purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, customs records, and end-user statements; sanctions and adverse-media screening; payment-flow diagram; explanation of any intermediary; and documented compliance approval before execution.
Expected export or import activity without a coherent customs, VAT, and transaction-reconciliation process.

Root cause: Expected export or import activity without a coherent customs, VAT, and transaction-reconciliation process.

Defense evidence: EORI registration where required; VAT registration details; sample commercial invoices; Incoterms; customs-broker agreement; transport documents; import and export workflow; inventory records; VAT and Intrastat procedures; bank reconciliation policy; and responsible-person matrix.
Multiple foreign accounts, use of personal accounts, payment-service-provider accounts, or unexplained transfers between affiliated entities.

Root cause: Multiple foreign accounts, use of personal accounts, payment-service-provider accounts, or unexplained transfers between affiliated entities.

Defense evidence: Treasury policy; approved account list; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing support; account-purpose matrix; monthly reconciliation procedures; evidence that personal accounts are not used for corporate receipts; and documented approval controls for intercompany payments.
Negative media, politically exposed person status, regulatory history, insolvency indicators, or adverse information concerning a director, shareholder, supplier, or customer.

Root cause: Negative media, politically exposed person status, regulatory history, insolvency indicators, or adverse information concerning a director, shareholder, supplier, or customer.

Defense evidence: Independent legal and compliance report; explanation and supporting court or regulatory documents; remediation evidence; enhanced-monitoring plan; updated corporate certificates; PEP declaration; wealth and income evidence; and senior-management approval of the residual-risk assessment.
Application for a capital account or capital certificate without a finalized incorporation deed, subscription details, or clear account signatory mandate.

Root cause: Application for a capital account or capital certificate without a finalized incorporation deed, subscription details, or clear account signatory mandate.

Defense evidence: Draft or executed articles; incorporation deed or notarial appointment; proposed name certificate; founders' identification; capital subscription schedule; bank account-opening mandate; source-of-funds evidence; notary instructions; and post-incorporation plan to convert or link the capital account to the operational account.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route capital through a regulated Spanish or EU bank using SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments where available and SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies. The payment reference should identify the Spanish SL, the legal basis, and the purpose, such as share-capital subscription, share premium, shareholder loan, or equity contribution. Before receipt, provide the bank with the subscription agreement or loan agreement, corporate resolutions, ownership and beneficial-owner data, source-of-funds evidence, and intended use of proceeds. For incorporation capital, obtain the bank certificate required by the notary or confirm the current notarial evidence route accepted by the relevant bank. After incorporation, record the contribution in the accounting books and statutory corporate records. Reconcile the remitter, payer, and beneficiary names; avoid unrelated third-party remitters; retain MT103 or ISO 20022 payment confirmation; and monitor applicable foreign-investment, external-transaction, tax, and statistical reporting. No general Spanish FX purpose-code regime applies to ordinary euro transfers, but the bank may require an internal payment purpose, supporting invoice, contract, or regulatory declaration.Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 for traditional single-payment international transfers where supported; banks are progressively migrating to ISO 20022 payment messages, including pacs.008, so payment instructions should follow the servicing bank's format. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through a regulated bank under UCP 600, with documentary collections under URC 522 where appropriate. Include accurate beneficiary, ultimate payer, invoice, purchase-order, Incoterms, goods description, customs, shipping, and tax information. Use bank guarantees or standby letters of credit only under documented contractual terms and approved facility limits. Reconcile payments against invoices and goods-receipt or shipping evidence, apply segregation of duties and dual authorization, and retain records for tax, customs, AML, accounting, and audit purposes. Avoid cash settlement, personal accounts, unapproved payment agents, and third-party payments without documented commercial justification.Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forwards with a regulated bank or eligible investment firm, used to hedge identifiable forecast or contracted receivables, payables, capital injections, or intercompany flows.Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility restrictions, where offered by an appropriately regulated counterparty and permitted under the laws governing the currency and transaction.Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, valuation, collateral, accounting, and applicable EMIR obligations.Foreign-exchange options, including plain-vanilla calls, puts, and collars, for documented commercial exposures, subject to suitability, disclosure, premium, valuation, and treasury-policy controls.FX spot transactions and rolling short-dated conversions for operational settlement, provided the company maintains transaction records and does not conduct speculative dealing as an unlicensed financial business.All derivatives should be governed by an approved treasury policy and, where applicable, an ISDA or equivalent master agreement, confirmation procedures, counterparty limits, collateral terms, mark-to-market controls, hedge-accounting analysis, EMIR reporting or clearing assessment, and board-approved delegation limits.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium. An EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide EUR accounts, payment services, cards, and international transfers under passporting or local authorization, but it is not a Spanish deposit-taking bank unless separately licensed as a credit institution. Customer funds are generally safeguarded rather than covered by the Spanish deposit-guarantee scheme. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorization or a valid EU passport cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to the Spanish SL merely through an application interface. Fintech onboarding may be unsuitable for statutory share-capital certification, notarial incorporation evidence, complex shareholder loans, high-value trade finance, cash handling, documentary letters of credit, or transactions involving elevated sanctions, marketplace, or virtual-asset exposure. The company should maintain a regulated Spanish or EU bank as its primary treasury account and use an EMI only as a controlled secondary rail.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de cuentas anuales) Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting, and approval is required within six months of the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year companies, the last practical filing date is 31 July of the following year. $280 USD If accounts are not filed within 18 months from the fiscal year-end, the registry sheet is closed (cierre registral), preventing registration of any corporate acts (e.g., director reappointments, capital changes, amendments). The company may also face administrative dissolution for continued non-filing. Fiscal penalties and surcharges may apply under tax law.
Beneficial ownership annual confirmation (Declaración de titularidad real) Annually within one month after the anniversary of the prior registration or upon any change in beneficial ownership, as applicable under Royal Decree 571/2023; the calendar deadline is typically due within 30 days after each annual confirmation trigger. $75 USD Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership declarations may result in fines up to EUR 60,000 under Spanish money-laundering / beneficial-ownership regulations, and the entity may be prohibited from using certain corporate registry services until compliance is restored.
Annual return deadline

Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting, and approval is required within six months of the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year companies, the last practical filing date is 31 July of the following year.

Late filing penalties

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: Mandatory audit is required for companies meeting at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. Companies in certain sectors (e.g., banks, insurers, investment funds) are always audited regardless of size.
